findings.location: Section 5, first bullet; Figure 3a (and its caption)
findings.quote: On the field-star calibration this corresponds to BP−RP ≈ 2.31 (1σ range 2.22–2.40, with a systematic of about ±0.1 mag), an M1.5–M2.5 dwarf. A K7 dwarf (BP−RP ≈ 1.65) would give about 1.35 arcsec, 5.7σ (statistical) below the measured shift.
findings.problem:
Three mutually inconsistent colour calibrations are used without saying so:
(1) Section 4 gives only the linear k = 1.52 arcsec/mag. With it, 2.94 arcsec gives BP−RP = 0.786 + 2.94/1.52 = 2.72 (≈M3.5), not 2.31.
(2) Figure 3a plots the 2,560-fit calibration. That curve has no stars between BP−RP 1.9 and 2.3, and its bin at BP−RP 2.35 sits at 3.31 arcsec, above the 2.94 ± 0.28 band. Read off the plotted curve, 2.94 arcsec gives about 2.22, the lower 1σ edge. The vertical band at 2.22–2.40 therefore does not follow from the plotted points.
(3) The 2.31 actually comes from the unplotted wide sample (≈5,560 fits).
On top of this, the K7 expectation (1.35 arcsec) uses the linear k, while the M-dwarf read-off uses the steeper empirical curve. A referee checking the figure will see that it does not support the stated colour.
findings.evidence:
localise/v3/results/f02_colour_theta.json (the curve plotted by make_figures.py lines 212–220): bins C=1.687 → 1.464 arcsec (n=31), then C=2.349 → 3.308 arcsec (n=8), with no 1.9–2.3 bin. Linear interpolation gives 1.687 + (2.94−1.464)/(3.308−1.464)×0.662 = 2.22.
f02_colourw_theta.json (wide sample): 2.139 → 2.418 arcsec (n=21) and 2.422 → 3.29 arcsec (n=21). Interpolating there gives 2.31; this is the source of the localise_v3 key number 'BP−RP 2.14 → −2.42″; 2.42 → −3.29″ (linear prediction −2.55″)'.
On the same wide curve, BP−RP 1.65 gives 1.45 arcsec, i.e. (2.94−1.45)/0.28 = 5.3σ. Mamajek's K7V (EEM_dwarf.txt) has BP−RP = 1.70, which gives about 1.55 arcsec, i.e. 5.0σ.
findings.fix:
Plot the wide-sample curve (f02_colourw_theta.json) in Fig. 3a and label it '≈5,560 fits'. Alternatively, keep the 2,560-fit curve and quote BP−RP ≈ 2.2.
Replace the text with: 'The colour shift is not linear at the red end: field stars at BP−RP 2.14 and 2.42 are shifted by 2.42 and 3.29 arcsec, against 2.1 and 2.5 arcsec from the linear coefficient. Read off this empirical curve, the deep-eclipse shift of 2.94 ± 0.28 arcsec gives BP−RP ≈ 2.31 (1σ range 2.22–2.40; systematic ±0.1–0.2 mag), an M1.5–M2.5 dwarf. A K7 dwarf (BP−RP ≈ 1.70) would be shifted by about 1.5 arcsec, about 5σ (statistical) below the measured value.'

findings.location: Section 5, third bullet; Figure 3b grey W1 box
findings.quote: The deep-eclipse depth is 3.7 ± 1.1 times the TESS depth (S/N 4.3), against 0.70–1.15 for an eclipsed G/F star.
findings.problem: The quoted G/F range for W1 leaves out the campaign's own most-favourable G/F case (5,600 K, grazing), which predicts W1/TESS = 1.35. findings.problem: The sentence sits in the bullet arguing for a bound triple, so it reads as evidence of binding. In the odds analysis the Gaia signature has likelihood factor 1 for bound against chance-aligned, because both hypotheses predict the same unresolved companion. The final referee also notes that the unexplained VHS source at 1.12 arcsec could itself produce the signature. The Gaia signature constrains separation, not association.

findings.quote: With e sin ω free and no main-sequence term, the light curve allows a larger light fraction (about 7%).
findings.problem: This implies the light curve bounds the pair's light at roughly 7% or less. In fact the shape sets no useful upper limit: the profile is flat from about 2.5% to 18%. The uniform-prior posterior with e sin ω free prefers about 7%; it is not an upper bound. Larger light fractions are excluded only by the main-sequence requirement, the ellipsoidal limit, the colours and the SED. Section 6.1 mentions only the lower limit, so a reader may assume the upper side is constrained.

Solutions with f >= 4% need chi2_MS >= 12. SED limit <= 5.8-11.6%.
findings.fix: Replace with: 'The light-curve shape alone gives only a lower limit (f > 2.2%). With e = 0 its likelihood is flat from about 2.8% to 15%, and with e sin ω free a uniform-prior fit prefers about 7%. Larger light fractions are excluded only by the main-sequence requirement (χ²_MS ≥ 12 at f ≥ 4%), the ellipsoidal limit, the colours and the SED (≤ 5.8–11.6%).'

'BEB' means different things to different ExoFOP users.

- In TRICERATOPS and vespa, and in other ExoFOP users' notes, BEB means a background (chance-aligned) EB. That is exactly the hypothesis this report argues against. The bound case is TRICERATOPS SEB/SEBx2P (vespa HEB).

In TFOP SG1 shorthand: EB (photometric BEB, i.e. a blended EB; this does not mean a background star here; in TRICERATOPS terms the favoured scenario is SEBx2P).'

findings.quote: If the G star (1.03 M☉) were eclipsed by a companion in a 1.30 d orbit, even a 0.1 M☉ companion would give it a radial-velocity semi-amplitude K ≥ 18 km s−1.
findings.problem: There is a logical gap: the report never says why a companion of at least 0.1 M☉ is required. A sceptic will ask about a brown-dwarf or planetary companion, which would give K ≲ 10 km/s and be consistent with the 9.9 km/s peak-to-peak scatter. The missing step is the secondary eclipse. A 2,600 ppm secondary (45% of the primary depth) requires a self-luminous companion with about 45% of the eclipsed star's TESS surface brightness, so the true minimum K is far above 18 km/s.

For 0.1 M☉, K1 = 17.97 km/s (also referee_all_result.json).
findings.fix: Insert before the RV sentence: 'The 2,600 ppm secondary eclipse (45% of the primary depth) requires a self-luminous companion with roughly 45% of the eclipsed star's TESS surface brightness. For an eclipsed G star this means a K dwarf of about 0.7 M☉ (K ≈ 95 km s⁻¹). Even a 0.1 M☉ companion would give K ≥ 18 km s⁻¹.'

findings.fix: '...shows that at least one component (most likely the spotted primary) rotates synchronously, as expected for a tidally locked 1.3-d binary.'

I cropped and inspected the summary box, Tables 1–5, the Section 3 and 6.3 text, and the Table 4/5 subscript areas. I viewed fig1_lightcurve.png, fig2_localisation.png and fig3_colour.png at full resolution. Against the data: I checked the Fig 2 offsets and the VHS-residual position angle in localise/v3/results/s05_baseline.json, the Fig 3a calibration curve in f02_colour_theta.json (per-bin star counts, linear vs binned values), and the per-product depth scales behind Fig 1b in lcmodel/v6/results/depths_by_product.json. findings.location: Page 4, Figure 3a, with page 3, Section 5 first bullet and Section 4 end of paragraph 1
findings.quote: On the field-star calibration this corresponds to BP−RP ≈ 2.31 (1σ range 2.22–2.40, with a systematic of about ±0.1 mag), an M1.5–M2.5 dwarf.
findings.problem: The only calibration the text gives is linear: 1.52 arcsec per magnitude. On that slope, a 2.94 arcsec shift gives Δ(BP−RP) = 1.93, i.e. BP−RP ≈ 2.72, not 2.31. The value 2.31 is read off the binned field-star curve, which steepens at the red end. That curve has no bin at all between BP−RP 1.9 and 2.3, and only 8 stars at 2.3–2.7 and 3 at 2.7–3.2. Figure 3a shows this (the horizontal band crosses the linear trend near 2.7), but neither the text nor the caption says it. A reader will find the numbers contradict each other.
findings.evidence: f02_colour_theta.json 'curve': the bin at 1.6–1.9 has n = 31, the bin at 2.3–2.7 has n = 8 (rad −3.31 against a linear prediction of −2.37), the bin at 2.7–3.2 has n = 3, and there is no 1.9–2.3 bin. localise_v3_result.json: "Steeper at the red end ... 2.42 → −3.29 ± 0.11" (linear prediction −2.55")" and "Systematic about ±0.1 mag from the few red calibrators".
findings.fix: Section 5: "The field-star relation steepens for red stars (Figure 3a), so the linear coefficient does not apply here. Reading the shift off the binned relation gives BP−RP ≈ 2.31 (1σ range 2.22–2.40; systematic about ±0.1 mag, because only 11 calibration stars are redder than BP−RP 1.9), an M1.5–M2.5 dwarf." Add to the Figure 3a caption: "The relation steepens above BP−RP ≈ 1.9, where only 11 calibration stars are available (none at 1.9–2.3)."

draft:1.rationale:
The note is 894 characters, counted with Python. That includes the single newline between the two paragraphs, which the ExoFOP editor stores as
. Two of the three style studies recommend 450-900 characters for this kind of note and the third recommends 650-1200, so 894 sits at the top of the stricter range. If [file/tag] is replaced by a full ExoFOP filename such as TIC71316387.01O-xx20261016-EB-vetting.pdf, the note grows to about 930 characters. That is still well inside the analogue range (median 916) and far below the ~4,000-character cap. Structure follows the TFOP analytic-prose model (quinn, hartman, latham triples): - The verdict and the 2x-period statement come first. - The ephemeris follows, with its time system and data sources. - Each line of evidence gets one clause with one number, strongest first: eclipse depths, then the G star's constant RV, then the centroid limit with the catalogued neighbours excluded, then the eclipse colours and light fraction. - Next is the hedged interpretation and a suggested disposition in community wording ("Suggest FP/EB"; no "Retired as" or Master Disp syntax). - It closes with a concrete follow-up request, a statement of what is not needed, and a pointer to the uploaded file. Every number comes from the verified/audited facts: - P = 1.30367228 +/- 0.00000019 d and T0 = BJD_TDB 2460165.67042 +/- 0.00018 are the adopted fit. It uses only TESS-SPOC S1/S28/S68 and the campaign's own re-barycentred TESScut S95/S105/S106 times, with no QLP time stamps, so the QLP S103-105 barycentric bug does not affect it. - The early QLP-biased ephemeris (1.3036712 d) is not used. - Depths are 5770/2600 ppm, with the secondary at phase 0.5. - The CTOI epoch falls on an EB secondary, which warns observers not to schedule on the CTOI ephemeris. - The Gaia RV is given in the audit-corrected form: 15 RVS transits over 946 d, not 15 epochs. - The source lies within 1.24 arcsec (95%), and every resolved Gaia neighbour is excluded (the lesson from the sabin retraction). - SuperWASP depths are shallower and W1 depths deeper than TESS. The pair contributes ~2.6% of TESS flux, flagged as an MS-model estimate rather than dynamical. - Predicted delta-Ks is ~2.6 mag and the separation is likely below 0.9 arcsec. Overclaiming is avoided: the triple is "likely ... unconfirmed", and the chance-alignment odds are given as "improbable" rather than as a figure. I left out the odds number because it depends on the priors (worst case ~200), professional notes use no e-notation, and the PDF gives the full grid. Formatting is safe for the ExoFOP export: - Plain ASCII only: "+/-", "arcsec", "delta-Ks". - No double-quote character, so the export cannot drop an arcsec mark. - No bare < or > (I wrote "below 0.9 arcsec"). - No Markdown, no signature, no email. The note does not mention AI. The corpus has no precedent for it, and disclosure goes in the PDF. Neither the QLP pipeline issue nor TIC 214311908 is mentioned. The draft text is also saved at /obsnote/wf/note_draft/note_v4.txt. Nothing was submitted or posted, and no repo files were modified.

draft:3.rationale:
Length: 1197 characters, measured with Python (ASCII only, so it is also 1197 bytes). It is one paragraph of 10 sentences. That sits at the top of the 650-1200 range the closest-analogue study gives for multi-part EB and source-attribution notes (median 916, IQR 804-1375). It is longer than the 450-900 range for single-thread notes, as expected for a note making five separate arguments. It stays below the ~1,300-1,800 level where community notes start to read like reports and have needed corrections.

Structure follows the TFOP/community house style:
1. Verdict and 2x period in the first sentence, with the CTOI named.
2. Ephemeris: P and T0 with errors in BJD_TDB, and the source products/sectors.
3. Evidence, one clause and one number each, strongest first: alternating depths on the same parity in all six sectors; the constant Gaia DR3 RV against the K of 18 km/s or more required if the G star were eclipsed; the colour-corrected centroid within 1.24 arcsec (95%), with resolved neighbours explicitly excluded (the lesson of the sabin retraction); the SuperWASP/W1 colour of the eclipses.
4. Hedged interpretation: 'probably', 'likely', 'prior-dependent', 'unconfirmed'.
5. Suggested disposition, worded as 'We suggest FP (blended EB)', not SG1 'Retired as'/'Master Disp'.
6. Concrete follow-up with predicted contrasts and separation.
7. A pointer to the upload, with the [file/tag] placeholder.

Every number comes from the verified/audited facts:
- P 1.30367228 +/- 0.00000019 d.
- T0 BJD_TDB 2460165.67042 +/- 0.00018.
- 5770/2600 ppm.
- RV -6.07 +/- 0.86 km/s over 946 d (no '15 epochs' wording).
- K1 of 18 km/s or more.
- 1.24 arcsec (95%).
- Gaia neighbours at 18-55 arcsec.
- ~2.6% light fraction.
- M1-M2.5V + M4-M4.5V types.
- Odds 1e3-1e4, written as plain numbers with the direction stated.
- delta-Ks ~2.6 and ~3.8 mag at 832 nm.
- Separation below 0.9 / 0.1 arcsec.

The ephemeris uses only TESS-SPOC and TESScut times. No QLP S103-105 time stamps are used, so the barycentric bug does not affect it and the note does not need to mention it. Saying that the CTOI epoch is a secondary eclipse stops observers scheduling on the CTOI ephemeris.

Deliberately left out:
- Masses: they are not dynamical and are better in the PDF, so only model-based spectral types are given, hedged.
- Undiluted depths, K1/K2 predictions, the Gaia IPD diagnostics, the drift of the CTOI ephemeris, and method details. All of these go in the PDF.

Formatting and other conventions:
- No double-quote or '<'/'>' characters, which avoids the export and HTML problems found in the corpus. Units are written 'arcsec', '+/-' and 'delta-Ks'; there is no Unicode and no Markdown.
- No signature, email or AI mention (the corpus has no precedent for AI disclosure; per the brief, disclosure goes in the PDF).

issues.quote: Eclipse colours (TESS centroid shift, SuperWASP, NEOWISE W1) suggest an ~M2V + ~M4V pair with ~2.6% of TESS flux (MS-model estimates).
issues.problem: This credits the colours with more than they show. (1) Only the TESS colour shift gives about M2 (BP-RP 2.31, M1.5-M2.5). The SuperWASP and W1 depth ratios give an eclipsed-star Teff of 4040 +330/-280 K, i.e. K7-M0, and the final referee says late-K (K5-K7) is 'disfavoured by the TESS colour shift but allowed by the archival depth ratios'. The README also says 'possibly late-K'. (2) The ~M4V secondary, the 2.6% light fraction and the spectral types come mainly from the light-curve shape fitted with main-sequence relations, not from the colours. The campaign's own draft said 'eclipse colours and shape'. The only model-independent result is the lower limit of 2.2% or more from the shape.
issues.fix: 'Eclipse colours (TESS centroid shift, SuperWASP, NEOWISE W1) show a red, early-M (possibly late-K) eclipsed star; the light-curve shape under MS relations gives an ~M2V + ~M4V pair with ~2.6% of TESS flux (>=2.2% from shape alone).'

issues.quote: Likely a bound triple (chance alignment disfavoured ~1000-10000x, prior-dependent), unconfirmed.
issues.problem: The range does not match the final referee's numbers. Baseline variants give 5.1e3-1.4e4 (median 8.2e3), so the baseline median is near the top of the stated range and its upper end goes beyond it. The full set of 160 variants gives 5.8e2-3.8e4, and the worst case is about 200. A floor of '~1000' hides the 200-600 cases, and 'prior-dependent' does not say how far the number can fall.
issues.fix: 'Likely a bound hierarchical triple: a bound companion is favoured over chance alignment by ~5000-14000x for baseline priors (>~200x in the worst case); unconfirmed.' A shorter alternative: '... by of order 10^4 (worst case ~200)'.

issues.quote: Gaia DR3 RV constant over 946 d (15 RVS transits, chi2 p = 0.28) vs K of 18 km/s or more if it were.
issues.problem: Each number checks out: rv_chisq_pvalue 0.2751, rv_time_duration 945.6 d, rv_nb_transits 15, and K1 = 17.96 km/s for a 0.1 Msun partner with Mtot 1.13. But the note does not say where 18 km/s comes from: it is the floor for a 0.1 Msun eclipsing partner at sin i ~ 1. It also does not say that the 15 transits fall in only 12 visibility periods (6 of them deblended). A reader who looks up rv_amplitude_robust = 9.9 km/s could take that as variability, although it matches the ~2.6 km/s per-transit noise.
issues.fix: 'Gaia DR3 RV constant (15 RVS transits in 12 visibility periods over 946 d; chi2 p = 0.28), whereas any >=0.1 Msun eclipsing partner would give K >= 18 km/s.'

issues.quote: Colour-corrected difference-image centroids put the EB within 1.24 arcsec of the G star (95%)
issues.problem: 1.24 arcsec is the baseline 95.45% limit. It depends on a colour-correction model calibrated on only 13-45 field stars redder than BP-RP 2 (4 beyond 2.7). The shallow-eclipse colour (BP-RP >~ 3) is extrapolated beyond that calibration, and across the 16 analysis variants the 95% limit runs from 1.06 to 1.54 arcsec. Giving one number with no range overstates the precision. 'Centroids' are also really PRF fits to stacked difference images, which is acceptable shorthand.
issues.fix: '...within 1.24 arcsec of the G star (95%; 1.06-1.54 arcsec across analysis variants; >=1.5 arcsec excluded at p = 0.002)'. Or keep 1.24 and give the variant range in the PDF.
